standard.title: Design personalised activity plans
standard.description: participate in physical activities designed to enhance health, wellbeing and fitness, and design, apply and evaluate strategies for incorporating these activities into their lives
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can design and justify strategies to increase physical activity to achieve health and wellbeing outcomes (AC9HP8M06). At Y9-10 the focus shifts to personalisation — designing, applying and evaluating strategies that incorporate specific physical activities into their own lives, including understanding individual physiological responses.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students participate in fitness-enhancing activities, design personalised strategies for incorporating them into their lives, and evaluate those strategies against fitness and wellbeing goals.

nodes.label: Understanding individual physiological responses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate their body's responses to physical activity at different intensities and connect these to fitness components
nodes.minimum_width: Participate in a physical activity and identify at least two physiological responses (e.g. heart rate, breathing rate, ability to talk, recovery rate); explain what each response indicates
nodes.typical_width: Participate in a range of physical activities and evaluate individual responses including heart rate, breathing rate, ability to talk and recovery rate; perform activities designed to improve fitness and analyse how each improves specific fitness components
wider: Investigate target training heart-rate zones for different individuals — explain how these zones are measured, how they relate to fitness level, and how they should inform activity selection for different health goals
Compare physiological responses across different activity types at the same perceived effort level — evaluate what this reveals about relative fitness demands
Analyse how individual factors (age, fitness level, health condition) affect physiological responses to the same activity — evaluate what this means for personalised plan design
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot interpret their own physiological responses to physical activity cannot make evidence-based decisions about activity selection and intensity in their personalised plan (Node 2) — the design requires understanding what the body is signalling during and after activity.

response_modes.reason: Students often participate in activities and report physiological responses without interpreting what they mean. The structured reasoning investment is in building the interpretation chain: this response occurred, it indicates this physiological state, this implies this about fitness demand or intensity level, therefore this about activity design. Heart rate zones add a quantitative framework that supports this reasoning.

success_criteria: Names at least two physiological responses observed during activity
Explains what each response indicates about exertion level or fitness demand
Connects at least one response to a specific fitness component (e.g. cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength)

nodes.label: Designing and evaluating personalised plans
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can design, apply and evaluate a personalised strategy for incorporating physical activity into their life
nodes.minimum_width: Design a personalised physical activity plan with at least one realistic goal; apply it for a period and evaluate whether it achieved the goal
nodes.typical_width: Set realistic physical activity goals; design, implement and evaluate a personalised program incorporating regular physical activity into weekly routines; justify the selection of activities linked to goals and wellbeing outcomes; use digital tools to design, monitor and adjust the plan
wider: Design a personalised plan that incorporates target heart-rate zones for different workout types — justify intensity choices with reference to fitness goals and physiological evidence
Evaluate a personalised plan across a multi-week implementation — track progress against goals and make documented adjustments; evaluate what factors supported or hindered adherence
Design a personalised plan for a different person (e.g. a family member with different fitness goals) — justify the adaptations made and evaluate what personalisation required

response_modes.reason: Designing and evaluating personalised plans builds through the cycle of planning, implementing, evaluating, and adjusting. A single design exercise without implementation and evaluation is insufficient — students need experience of the full cycle, including what happens when a plan is harder to adhere to than expected. The digital tools direction supports ongoing monitoring rather than one-off evaluation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Heart-rate zone justified planning, multi-week tracked implementation, and designing for a different person each add a dimension that single-plan design does not. Students who engage the wider tier develop planning capability that accounts for real implementation factors — not just the ideal plan on paper.
success_criteria: Plan includes at least one specific, measurable goal
Activity selection is justified with reference to the goal and individual physiological needs
Evaluation addresses whether the goal was achieved and identifies at least one factor that affected adherence or outcome
